duration: Optional · choose a question or complete the set
intro: Complete your normal You Do first. For each map, show the largest useful groups, write a minimal expression and check the corresponding gates.

questions.title: One pair, one term
questions.prompt: A three-input logic circuit has the Karnaugh map below. Identify the largest valid group of 1s, write a simplified expression for Q, and name the gates required.

groups.label: One pair
groups.explanation: A stays 0 and C stays 1; B changes. Keep ¬A and C.

steps: Circle the two adjacent 1s in the top row.
A is always 0, so retain ¬A. C is always 1, so retain C. B changes, so remove B.
Gate plan: apply NOT to A, then AND with C.
marksBreak: 1 mark: correct NOT and AND gate plan.

questions.title: Opposite edges are neighbours
questions.prompt: The two outside columns contain 1s. Show the largest possible group, give a simplified expression for Q and explain the equivalent gate circuit. Why is this grouping allowed?

groups.label: One group across opposite edges
groups.explanation: The left and right columns are adjacent through wraparound. A and B change; C stays 0.

steps: All four outer 1s form ONE group of four. The outside columns are neighbours.
A varies between rows; B varies between columns. C remains 0, so ¬C is the only term.
Gate plan: a single NOT gate on C.
marksBreak: 1 mark: correct wraparound group of four.
1 mark: explain why the opposite edges are neighbours.

questions.title: Overlap is allowed
questions.prompt: This four-variable K-map represents a logic circuit. Show the two largest useful groups, write a minimal sum-of-products expression for Q, and describe an equivalent gate circuit.

groups.label: Orange 2 × 2 group
groups.explanation: A stays 0 across columns 00/01; D stays 1 across rows 01/11. Term: ¬A ∧ D.

groups.label: Blue group of four
groups.explanation: On row CD=11, C and D stay 1. Term: C ∧ D. Some cells belong to both groups.

steps: Orange block: rows 01/11 and columns 00/01. Keep ¬A and D.
Blue row: all four columns of row 11. Keep C and D.
Gate plan: NOT A; two AND gates for (¬A,D) and (C,D); OR the outputs.
marksBreak: 1 mark: join the terms with OR (or equivalent correct gate plan).

questions.title: The four corners connect
questions.prompt: Show the two largest groups on this four-variable K-map, including wraparound in both directions. Find a minimal sum-of-products expression for Q and explain why A and C disappear.

groups.label: Orange wraparound corners
groups.explanation: Four corners form ONE group. B = 0 and D = 0 remain fixed: ¬B ∧ ¬D.

groups.label: Blue central block
groups.explanation: The central four 1s form one group. B = 1 and D = 1 remain fixed: B ∧ D.

steps: Group the four corners as one wraparound block across both pairs of opposing edges.
Group the central four 1s as a second block.
A and C change within both groups, so they disappear. B and D are the only constant inputs.
Gate plan: (NOT B AND NOT D) OR (B AND D).
marksBreak: 1 mark: combine the two groups with OR.
1 mark: explain why A and C disappear.
